title: Organization Configuration — the adopted Template — contract v1
description:
The Organization's view of its own adopted Template. SHAPES ONLY; the rulings are in tenant-configuration-v1.contract.yaml.

REQUEST CLASS: tenant-admin (docs/decisions/0044).

*** THIS SET WAS SCOPED AS 'TEMPLATE AND INSTALLED-APP CONFIGURATION' AND PUBLISHES ONLY THE FIRST HALF, AS ONE READ. *** The App half is REFUSED — there is no App runtime, no manifest-admission path and no installed App anywhere in Dudo, so a configuration shape published now would be designing the App model from a settings screen. See the contract's theAPPHALFISREFUSED. That refusal is the larger part of this contract's value.

AND THE TENANT CANNOT CHANGE ITS TEMPLATE. Adoption is `core.platform-organization.set-template`, `platform` scope, an operator act. This contract publishes a READ and no write at all.

NOT EXECUTED. Normative and hand-checked.

adoptedTemplate.description:
The Template this Organization has adopted, as the Organization sees it.

*** IT REFERENCES `template-v1`'s DEFINITIONS RATHER THAN RESTATING THEM, AND THAT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN USUAL: A TEMPLATE'S LABELS RENDERED DIFFERENTLY ON TWO SURFACES WOULD BE THE SAME ORGANIZATION CALLED TWO THINGS. *** The operator console reads `template-v1`; this is what the customer's own console reads; one set of definitions keeps them the same words.

*** NO `status`, AND ITS ABSENCE IS A DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY WITH THE OPERATOR VIEW. *** `template-v1`'s `templateOutput` carries one, because retirement is an operator concern: it blocks NEW adoption. **An Organization that has already adopted a retired Template keeps it and keeps rendering its labels** — `core.template.retire`'s own entry says so — so the status changes nothing the customer can act on, and showing it would invite a question ('is ours being withdrawn?') whose answer is no and whose route to ask does not exist.

NO `created_at`, NO ADOPTION DATE, NO OPERATOR IDENTITY. Who set this Organization's Template and when is an operator-action fact; it lives in `platform_operator_action` and in the tenant's own audit trail, and putting it here would make a configuration read a partial audit feed.

template.description:
The adopted Template, or null.

*** NULL IS THE ORDINARY CASE AND NOT AN ERROR. *** `organization.template_id` is nullable and onboarding does not require one; an Organization with no Template renders Dudo's own default vocabulary. **A client must render null as the default structure rather than as 'not configured'** — the second reads as a setup step the customer cannot perform, because adoption is an operator act and there is no tenant route to it.

AND A CLIENT MUST NOT OFFER A PICKER. There is nothing for a tenant to choose from: listing Templates is `core.template.list` at `platform` scope, which no tenant role can hold.

getConfigurationOutput.description:
The Organization's configuration.

*** ONE FIELD, AND THE SHAPE IS AN OBJECT RATHER THAN THE TEMPLATE ITSELF SO THAT IT CAN GROW WITHOUT A VERSION. *** Installed-App configuration, when there is such a thing, is a second field here and is additive (API_STANDARD.md §6). Returning the Template alone at the top level would make the App half a breaking change to a shape that had no reason to be narrow.

**That is the one accommodation this contract makes for a capability that does not exist**, and it is a shape decision rather than a content one — no App field is declared, named, or reserved.
